meta.title: Now indicator
meta.description: The marker that says where the present moment falls, when it is shown, and what keeps it moving.

basics.intro: A schedule is read against the present: what has passed, what is running, what is still ahead. The now indicator draws that boundary — a labelled line across the timeline grid, a marker between the cards in the list.
basics.when: It is shown only when all of these hold, so it never claims a position it does not have:
points: enableNowIndicator is on, which it is by default.
The day being read is not in the past.
Now falls inside the current shift, and inside the rendered range.
The day being read is the day now falls in.

clock.intro: The component keeps its own clock, ticking every nowTickInterval while it is mounted and pausing while the document is hidden — a schedule left open in a background tab costs nothing. Pass now to take the clock over: a test, a screenshot or a replay then shows the moment you choose instead of the moment it is.

points: In the list the marker is a separator with a label, so the boundary is announced and not only drawn.
In the timeline the line is decorative: the same time is in its label pill and in every card’s name.
The marker does not move focus and does not scroll anything; where a view lands is <link to="/navigation/">landing</link>, a separate decision.
The parts nowMarker in the list and nowLine with nowLabel in the timeline are replaceable through slots.
--rs-color-now is the color of the line and of its label.
localization.now.label is the text, and formatters.clockTime the time in it.
enableNowIndicator turns it off entirely, for a schedule that is not about today.
One marker at a time: only the current shift gets one, even when several shifts of the same day are rendered.
The clock ticks at a fixed interval rather than exactly on the minute, so the marker can lag by up to one interval.
There is no "now" in a time zone other than the reader’s.
